construction_markdown:
Let `p(Z)=Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1`, `F=F_2[Z]/(p)`, and `α=Z mod p`. Represent field elements in the ordered basis `(1,α,…,α^15)`.

Set `A=span_F2{1,α,…,α^14}` and `Y=F_2^15`, both in little-endian binary order. Let `M=F[X]_{≤64}`, with binary basis `{α^iX^j: 0≤j≤64, 0≤i≤15}`.

For `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15}z_iα^i` and `y=(y_1,…,y_15)`, define `h_y(z)=z_0+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`. For `(a,y)∈A×Y`, define the functional `ℓ_{a,y}∈M*` by `ℓ_{a,y}(f)=h_y(f(a))`. The connection set is `D={ℓ_{a,y}:(a,y)∈A×Y}`.

The code is the character code

`C={c_f=(ℓ_{a,y}(f))_{(a,y)∈A×Y}:f∈M}`.

Equivalently, it is generated by the rows `c_{α^iX^j}`. There is no sampling, search, puncturing, shortening, repetition, or padding.

distance_audit: For each field symbol `z`, the inner signed sum over `Y` is `2^15` for `z=0`, `−2^15` for `z=1`, and zero otherwise.
Thus the Cayley eigenvalue associated with `f` is `λ_f=2^15(N_0(f)−N_1(f))`.
For every nonconstant `f` of degree at most 64, both `f` and `f−1` have at most 64 roots, so `|λ_f|≤64·2^15=2^21`.
The nonzero constants are handled separately: `f=1` is the all-one word, while every other nonzero constant has weight `2^29`. Hence every nonzero codeword is covered.
The fixed subspace polynomial `L_U`, for `U=span{1,…,α^5}`, has 64 zeros on `A` and never takes value 1 there. Its word therefore has exact weight `(32768−64)16384=535,822,336`.

Independent finite-field recomputation reproduced the stated Frobenius residues, subspace-polynomial coefficients, nine image generators, 64 roots, zero occurrences of value 1, and exact target weight.
explicitness_audit: The modulus `p=0x1002d`, polynomial basis, message basis, evaluation space, row order, and column order are fixed symbolically.
Row `r=16j+i` and column `c=2^15q+s` have the direct entry formula `h_{y(s)}(α^i a(q)^j)`; no oracle or selected seed occurs.
The algorithm emits exactly `1040·2^30=1,116,691,496,960` bits, or exactly 130 GiB when bit-packed.
A carryless degree-16 multiplication and reduction uses fewer than 1,024 elementary bit operations. At most 80 such multiplications and fewer than 64 further operations compute any entry.
Including iteration and output, the entire matrix is emitted in fewer than `2^28 n` elementary bit operations, hence in deterministic `n^{O(1)}` time.
The exact-distance witness is fixed by a displayed subspace polynomial and separating functional, not by finite search.
The mixed-parity path emitter from the upstream handoff was not treated as a construction because no qualifying path indexer exists.
Repository publication validation could not run because `node` is unavailable and the workspace is read-only; this is workflow debt, not a theorem dependency.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Enumerate rows by `r=16j+i`, with `0≤j≤64` and `0≤i≤15`. Enumerate columns by `c=2^15q+s`, with `0≤q,s<2^15`; decode `q=Σ_{t=0}^{14}q_t2^t` and set `a=Σq_tα^t`, and decode `s=Σ_{t=1}^{15}y_t2^(t-1)`. Compute `z=α^i a^j` by carryless polynomial multiplication and reduction modulo `p=0x1002d`. If `z=Σz_tα^t`, output `G[r,c]=z_0 XOR XOR_{t=1}^{15}(z_t AND y_t)`. Stream entries in row-major order.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: Fewer than `2^28 n` elementary bit operations and `O(log n)` working bits beyond fixed 16-bit field registers; in particular `O(n)` at the fixed parameters.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: There are exactly `1040n` output entries. Naive exponentiation uses at most 64 multiplications for `a^j`, at most 15 for `α^i`, and one final multiplication. A schoolbook 16-by-16 carryless multiplication followed by reduction modulo the six-term degree-16 modulus uses fewer than 1,024 elementary bit operations. The affine dot product and loop maintenance use fewer than 64 further operations per entry. Thus the arithmetic cost is below `1040n(80·1024+64)<2^27n`; allowing another equal budget for counters and output gives `<2^28n`. This is polynomial and already accounts for every emitted bit.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters

`[1,073,741,824,1040,535,822,336]_2`.

It is the character code of an explicitly specified connected bipartite Cayley graph, and its complete generator matrix is emitted deterministically in polynomial time.

### 1. Field and construction

Put `p(Z)=Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1`. Direct reduction gives

`Z^(2^8)=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z (mod p)` and `Z^(2^16)=Z (mod p)`.

With `h=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3`, Euclidean division gives

`p=(Z^8+Z^7+Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^2+1)h+(Z^2+1)`

and

`h=(Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^3+Z^2+1)(Z^2+1)+1`.

Thus `gcd(p,Z^(2^8)−Z)=1`, while `p` divides `Z^(2^16)−Z`. The degree-16 Rabin criterion proves irreducibility. Hence `F=F_2[Z]/(p)` is the stated field.

Let `A`, `Y`, `M`, `h_y`, `ℓ_{a,y}`, `D`, and `C` be as defined in the construction. Every choice and ordering is fixed there.

### 2. Cayley set, length, linearity, and dimension

If `ℓ_{a,y}=ℓ_{a',y'}`, evaluation on all constant polynomials identifies the coefficient functionals `(1,y)` and `(1,y')`, so `y=y'`. Evaluation on all polynomials `zX` then gives `h_y(z(a−a'))=0` for every `z∈F`. If `a≠a'`, multiplication by `a−a'` is bijective, contradicting `h_y(1)=1`. Hence `a=a'`. Also `ℓ_{a,y}(1)=1`, so no connection element is zero.

Consequently `|D|=|A||Y|=2^30`. Since the ambient group has exponent two, `D=−D`; the Cayley graph is simple and undirected.

The map `f↦c_f` is binary linear. If `c_f=0`, then `h_y(f(a))=0` for every `y` and every `a`. The affine truth-table map `z↦(h_y(z))_y` is injective, so `f(a)=0` for all 32,768 points of `A`. A degree-at-most-64 polynomial with that many roots is zero. Thus the encoder is injective and

`dim C=dim_F2 M=65·16=1040`.

The same argument says that `D` spans `M*`, so the Cayley graph is connected.

### 3. Character spectrum and distance

For `z=Σz_iα^i`, affine balance gives

`Σ_{y∈Y}(−1)^{h_y(z)} = 2^15` if `z=0`, `−2^15` if `z=1`, and `0` otherwise.

For `b∈F`, write `N_b(f)=|{a∈A:f(a)=b}|`. The Cayley eigenvalue indexed by `f∈M` is therefore

`λ_f=Σ_{a,y}(−1)^{ℓ_{a,y}(f)}=2^15(N_0(f)−N_1(f))`.

If `f` is nonconstant, both `f` and `f−1` are nonzero polynomials of degree at most 64. Hence `N_0(f),N_1(f)≤64` and `|λ_f|≤2^21`. For constants, `f=0` gives the zero word, `f=1` gives the all-one word and eigenvalue `−2^30`, and every other nonzero constant gives eigenvalue zero. Thus every nonzero message is covered. Since

`wt(c_f)=(2^30−λ_f)/2`,

every nonzero word has weight at least `(2^30−2^21)/2=535,822,336`.

For equality without any search, let `U=span_F2{1,α,…,α^5}` and `L_U(X)=∏_{u∈U}(X−u)`. Subspace-polynomial recursion gives

`L_U=X^64+2e0cX^32+71eeX^16+d9a4X^8+2198X^4+c6caX^2+6115X`.

Its values on `α^6,…,α^14` are

`e9f1,d1b4,e1cf,9bc6,ea9c,7d5e,f733,26c1,770d`.

The binary functional with mask `0x007b` annihilates all nine values but takes value one on the field element 1. Because `L_U` is additive, this proves `1∉L_U(A)`. The polynomial has exactly its 64 defining roots in `U`; every other evaluation is nonzero and not 1. Its codeword therefore has weight exactly `(32768−64)2^14=535,822,336`.

### 4. Complete generator algorithm

Index rows by `(j,i)`, columns by `(a,y)`, and output

`G[(j,i),(a,y)]=h_y(α^i a^j)`.

These are precisely the evaluations of the binary basis `{α^iX^j}`, so the output is a full generator matrix. The algorithm in `generator_matrix` accounts for all `1040n` entries. Its conservative bound `<2^28n` bit operations is deterministic and polynomial in `n`; it uses only direct arithmetic modulo the displayed polynomial. This completes the explicitness proof.

proof_steps.proof: Affine balance gives the three inner sums. Root bounds for `f` and `f−1` yield `|λ_f|≤2^21` for all nonconstant messages; constants are checked separately.

theorem_statement: The explicitly indexed connection set `D⊂M*≅F_2^1040` has cardinality `2^30`. Its connected bipartite Cayley graph has eigenvalues `±2^30` and all remaining eigenvalues of magnitude at most `2^21`. The resulting binary character code has exact parameters `[2^30,1040,535822336]_2`, and the complete generator matrix is output deterministically in fewer than `2^28n` elementary bit operations.
